name: The majority voted in favour of a motion to pass the bill in the House of Representatives. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a third time. The bill will now be sent to the Senate for their consideration. This bill limits the circumstances in which the Minister has to the power to reconsider past decisions in order to create greater stability for certain projects. ### What does this bill do? According for the [explanatory memorandum](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Fems%2Fr7323_ems_129d226c-7198-4ca1-9f62-b01fdae1fa59%22;rec=0), which is a political document prepared by the Government, who introduced the bill: > *The 2021 State of the Environment Report made clear that all aspects of the Australian environment are under stress, and many are declining. Multiple pressures from factors like climate change, habitat loss, invasive species, and pollution create cumulative impacts that amplify threats to our environment.
